f: G T A six drops tomorrow. But what if your next open world... is Calgary?
You know these streets. Now you can walk them, drive them, and even fly over them, in a free game built on the real map of Calgary.
It's called Y Y C City Stories. It runs right in your web browser, with no download and no account.
Start with the map. The streets come from OpenStreetMap. The buildings, the parks, and even the shape of the ground mostly come from the City of Calgary's open data.
So when you drive down your own street, the homes are where they really are, fitted to their real footprint and height.

In and around downtown, the skyline is real too. Landmarks like Historic City Hall, The Bow, TELUS Sky and the Saddledome are built as their own detailed 3D models. And the Calgary Tower stands right where it should.
But the skyline is only the beginning. Wait until you see Stampede Park.
In this game, it's always Stampede time. There's a midway with a Ferris wheel and food booths, the Grandstand Show, a country music stage, and fireworks every night.
Next to the Saddledome, there's a concert of the game's own title song, Under One Sky. That's the song you're hearing right now.
Need to get around? Calgary Transit is in the game, with real bus routes and real stops from the City's own timetable.
Walk up to a stop, catch a bus, or ride the CTrain on the Red and Blue lines, right through downtown.
Now here's something a little different: real three one one requests.

Recent service requests from the City's open data show up as icons in the community where they were reported. Tap one to see what it's about, when it was reported, whether it's still open, and who's handling it.
And then, there are the stories.

Pick one of five characters. Ali, who just landed at Y Y C to start a new life. Natalia, a high school student who stands up to bullies. Chris, a seventy-two-year-old senior. Jean, who has lived in Martindale for years. And Leo, a visitor who arrives right in the middle of the Stampede.
Across twenty-seven missions, they learn how the city really works. How to pay a transit fare. Where newcomers can get free help. What Fair Entry and the public library offer.
How to sort your black, blue and green carts. Why you clear your sidewalk after it snows. When to call Health Link at eight one one. And how to spot a scam.
Natalia's story takes on bullying and cyberbullying, and it ends with a music video.
You can play in six languages: English, French, Punjabi, Urdu, Tagalog and Arabic, with voice lines in each one.
And when you just want to explore, there's free roam. Grab a car, call a helicopter, hunt for landmarks, or play online with other players.
So, is this G T A? No. G T A six comes out tomorrow on PlayStation five and Xbox Series X and S. If you're playing it, have fun!
Y Y C City Stories is something different: a small, free game about the city we actually live in. And you can play it today.
